transcript:
Header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-19 15:00 PDT
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Mariner Head of ML), Tom Ellis (Infra Lead), Priya Kapoor (Security)

Summary: quick discovery about Private / VPC deployment. customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private. heavy focus on networking, VPC peering, private endpoints, region residency, and key management.

Topics: Private VPC architecture, VPC peering patterns (cross-account), private endpoints vs VPC endpoints, NAT/egress control, region constraints, terraform automation, SOC2/KMS integration.

Transcript:
00:00 Sofia: All right hi everyone thanks for joining, i'm sofia from Redwood inference. can you hear me okay?
00:04 Aisha: Yep good, loud and clear. thanks for the invite.
00:06 Sofia: Cool i'll do a quick intro then daniel will jump into the networky setup — and we can dig into your constraints.
00:12 Daniel: Hi all, daniel here, i'm the solutions engineer. we'll try to map our private deployment options to your infra.
00:18 Tom: thanks. quick note, we're on AWS primarily, multi-account. looking to keep inference traffic inside our VPCs, minimal public egress.
00:26 Priya: and from security, we need KMS-integrated keys, audit logs, and SSO with our IdP — plus proof of SOC 2 readiness.
00:33 Sofia: Great. high level, Redwood supports three deployment modes: hosted API, dedicated capacity, and private (VPC/private endpoint). For the private offering we do a customer-controlled VPC peering or private link, you can run in your account or we can host in a customer VPC depending on the option. We'll use terms like private endpoints (VPC endpoints), VPC peering, cross-account peering — apologies if some names get swapped.
00:51 Aisha: When you say "run in our account" do you mean we'll host the inference nodes on our AWS account or is it more like private endpoint to your infra?
00:59 Daniel: both patterns are possible. option A: we deploy the Redwood runtime into your VPC / account — that's the fully private model with no public egress except what you permit. option B: we host in a dedicated VPC and we set up cross-account VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink to your VPC, so traffic flows over AWS backbone.
01:16 Tom: For us option A is preferable if we can keep it manageable. we want to own subnets and route tables. we don't want public IPs on inference nodes.
01:25 Daniel: Absolutely; we support private subnets, no public IP, and you can control NAT gateway egress. We also have a terraform module that sets up the subnets, security groups, and IAM roles; we can hand that to your infra team.
01:35 Aisha: latency is important — we'll be doing interactive chat and embeddings. are there region constraints? we need everything to be in us-west-2 ideally.
01:43 Sofia: That's fine, we support deployment in us-west-2. If you need multiple regions we can do cross-region replication, but that'll affect KV cache performance slightly.
01:52 Tom: cross-account peering — any limits on CIDR ranges, route propagation, or overlapping CIDRs? we have several /16s already used.
02:00 Daniel: Overlapping CIDRs are tricky — we require non-overlapping ranges for peering. For the in-account deployment that's not a problem since you're hosting the nodes inside your address space. For our hosted cross-account peering pattern we ask for a dedicated /22 or /23 subnet for the runtime, ideally routable from your app subnets.
02:15 Priya: on KMS, can we use our CMKs and HSM? encrypted volumes, and have you integrated with external key wraps?
02:22 Sofia: Yes, we integrate with customer-managed KMS keys. For Private deployments we can use your CMKs for disk and secret encryption and support HSM-backed keys depending on the cloud provider. we'll need the key ARN and a cross-account IAM permission set.
02:33 Priya: also need to see your audit logs retention and how traces are emitted. we can't have debug logs containing raw customer data sent off-prem.
02:41 Daniel: Good callout. Our private deployment has options to keep logs in your account or stream to your s3/bigquery. We can disable certain debug traces and redact sensitive spans; we'll share the logging config matrix.
02:52 Aisha: about private endpoints — do you use AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering? what's the recommended pattern?
02:58 Daniel: For low-latency, single-region workloads we often recommend in-account deployment. If you prefer us to host, AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) gives strong isolation and doesn't require route propagation changes, but it can add per-GB costs. VPC peering is straightforward but needs non-overlapping CIDRs and full route management. We can support either.
03:18 Tom: firewall / security groups — what ports do we need to open?
03:22 Daniel: Mostly port 443 for the API and some ephemeral ports for internal node communication. We'll provide a minimal SG template: allow 443 from your app subnets, allow control plane traffic from Redwood management IPs (or via designated endpoints), and block public ingress.
03:36 Sofia: Also mention egress control — if you require zero public egress we can run without NAT and route logs to your s3 via VPC endpoints. Some components like package updates may need controlled egress to specific repos; we can vendor images or bake AMIs to avoid external egress.
03:55 Priya: what about SSO / SAML and RBAC?
03:59 Sofia: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning and role-based access controls. For private deployments we can integrate with your IdP over outbound SAML with metadata exchange.
04:10 Aisha: curious about KV cache and state — will that live in the same VPC? if we push embeddings to a cache is that tenant-isolated?
04:18 Daniel: The KV cache is colocated with the runtime nodes and in the same VPC for private models. It's tenant-isolated by deployment — you can pin model variants per environment. For cross-region replication there are tradeoffs; we'll document expected token-latency differences.
04:31 Tom: automation — you mentioned terraform modules. how much is automated versus manual? we want infra-as-code.
04:36 Daniel: We provide opinionated Terraform modules for subnet, SGs, IAM roles, and the operator to bootstrap the runtime. The onboarding typically involves running the module, then a brief operator run to register the runtime with Redwood control plane (control plane endpoints can be private).
04:50 Aisha: what's the control plane connectivity story? does it phone home?
04:54 Daniel: The control plane needs to reach a registration endpoint; it can be via PrivateLink or a restricted egress to our control plane IPs. For fully air-gapped setups we offer an on-prem package but that adds deployment complexity.
05:06 Priya: regulatory wise, we have HIPAA-adjacent workloads. can you provide SOC2 report and pen test summaries?
05:12 Sofia: yes we'll share SOC2 and our standard security pack. For HIPAA workflows we recommend private deployment + customer-managed KMS and audit log retention in your account.
05:22 Aisha: pricing question — is private deployment priced differently than dedicated?
05:26 Sofia: Private deployments are typically enterprise licensing plus a monthly infra fee; dedicated is reserved capacity on our side with commit-based pricing. We'll share a custom quote after we know region, capacity, and model footprint.
05:38 Tom: for the pilot we want to run a small cluster in us-west-2 and run a benchmark for 100 concurrent chat sessions, measuring p95 latency and token cost.
05:47 Daniel: Great — we can size a pilot (2-4 GPUs) and run the benchmarks. we'll need sample workloads and a set of prompts.
05:54 Aisha: Ok next steps sound good. can you also include a checklist for network firewall rules and a sample terraform plan?
05:59 Sofia: Yes, action items captured. we'll follow up with architectures, security docs, terraform artifacts, and a proposed pilot schedule.
06:10 Tom: one more — any special notes about provider-specific stuff? we lean on EKS for other workloads. can the runtime sit in EKS or is it separate?
06:18 Daniel: Our runtime can run in Kubernetes or as EC2/GPU instances. We have a k8s operator for EKS if you'd prefer to integrate with your cluster. We'll include operator docs.
06:28 Priya: thanks everyone. that answers most of our questions.
06:31 Sofia: thanks all. we'll send the docs and propose dates.
06:34 Aisha: thanks, bye.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional word swaps ("V-P-C" vs "VPC", "K-V cache"), speaker interruptions, and some filler — we recommend consulting the attached architecture doc for canonical terms.
